outcome: Neurodevelopment at age 6 months (assessed using the Ages & Stages Questionnaire, 3rd Edition (ASQ-3))
Scores on the 5 ASQ-3 subdomains (gross motor, fine motor, communication, cognitive, personal-social)
cohort: 255 infants from the COVID-19 Mother Baby Outcomes Initiative at Columbia University Irving Medical Center in New York City (114 exposed to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection in utero, 141 unexposed), and a historical cohort of 62 infants born before the pandemic
finding: Birth during the COVID-19 pandemic, but not in utero exposure to maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection, was associated with lower scores on gross motor, fine motor, and personal-social development at age 6 months.
mod_finding: Infants born during the COVID-19 pandemic had significantly lower scores on measures of gross motor, fine motor, and personal-social development compared to a historical cohort, regardless of mode of delivery.
